data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English tréntan meaning 'to stretch, to turn'. The name Trenton has its origins in Old English and translates to 'town by the treent'. The name gained popularity during the Middle Ages due to the existence of various towns named Trent in England and the River Trent in Britain. The name Trenton carries the meaning “Town by the treent” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Trenton usually hope their child will grow to embody town by the treent and live with faith, good character and purpose.
